rv.q: High-octane burlesque spoof of the hit Sky TV series heightened by the raw talent on stage

Deep-Heat Rivalry commits to its stupidity admirably and, beneath all the bare flesh and denigration of British and American icons, contains considerably more wit than its trashy exterior might suggest.
Deep-Heat Rivalry is a firecracker of an evening.
With winning vocals, irreverent humour and sultry choreography, this adults-only panto is a riotous night, with joy (and filth) at its core.
It’s camp, cheeky, filthy, wonderfully daft and incredibly entertaining.
Deep-Heat Rivalry is an unforgettable night of fun!
DEEP-HEAT RIVALRY is funny, smartly written, and never lets you forget that you’re part of the action; a true cabaret.

For all its occasional chaos, Deep-Heat Rivalry remains a joyous, camp, queer, relevant and gloriously silly musical revue and TV parody that leaves audiences gasping for breath, whether from laughter or shock.
It had the feeling of an undergraduate production wanting to be outrageous but lacking any original ideas.
It's camp, rude, ridiculous and gloriously entertaining – and frankly, sometimes that's exactly what you want from a night at the theatre.
This show does exactly what it set out to do for its intended audience.
A thoroughly entertaining and winningly silly night out.

cn.t: Critics hail this raunchy musical parody as a hilarious riot, praising its powerhouse vocals, filthy humor, and energetic choreography. Most find it a joyous, no-holds-barred romp, though one critic notes it may alienate those unfamiliar with the source material.
